title: Samurai Jack
subtitle: all five seasons, in the source's episode order
blurb: Every episode of Genndy Tartakovsky's series — four seasons on Cartoon Network, then ten more in 2017.
notes: The 2017 season is season five, and the source says so five times.

A different network and thirteen years on is a fair reason to ask whether it is a separate show, so it was asked. The series infobox counts five seasons and 62 episodes; the episode list's series overview files it as season 5; the season article opens "The fifth and final season of Samurai Jack, an American animated series, premiered on Adult Swim's Toonami programming block"; its infobox numbers itself 5 with season 4 before it; and the overall numbering runs straight on from 52 to 53. Wikipedia does also call it a revival — the show "was revived thirteen years later with a darker, more mature fifth season that provided a conclusion to the series" — but a revival of this series, filed as its fifth season. So it is the fifth section here.
The network changed, and every season subtitle names its own.

Cartoon Network carried the first four seasons; the fifth went out on Adult Swim's Toonami block. Those are the only two networks the source's overview declares, and it carries the first forward until the second replaces it — which is read here rather than assumed. Cartoon Network Studios made all five; Williams Street assisted on the last.
The opening three are three rows.

The source files them in one block titled Samurai Jack: The Premiere Movie — which is the name of the VHS and DVD compilation the same article describes, not the name of an episode — and numbers them 1, 2 and 3 individually, with the part titles written into its summary. So the rows follow the numbering and carry those titles, and the compilation gets no row of its own. The two later two-parters are handled the same way and read Part I and Part II, because the source numbers their parts separately but does not title them separately.

Thirteen episodes in each of the four original seasons and ten in the fifth — 62 in all. Each season's count, first airdate and last airdate are checked against the source's own series overview before this builds, and the total against the series infobox.
The Roman numerals are the show's own episode numbers.

The source states the rule — episodes are identified in the credits by Roman numerals matching the running total, and the fifth season adds 40 so that LII (52) is followed by XCII (92) — so each row's numeral is derived from it and then checked against the source twice: the fifth season's ten titles are read back as numbers, and eight numeral-and-title pairs the series article spells out in its own citations have to match. Only the first four seasons carry a descriptive title as well, which is why the last ten rows are titled by numeral alone.
The order here is the numbering, not the broadcast.
Several episodes went out ahead of or behind their number — the fourth season began while the third was still airing. The list follows the source's numbering, which is the numbering the credits use.
Nothing is weighted, and hours are not tracked on this list.

Six sources were checked for a per-episode running time and between them they hold one for three of the 62. The episode tables carry no RunTime field on any of their 58 blocks; the fifth season's article has no runtime in its infobox; no episode has a Wikipedia article of its own, so there is no episode infobox and no Wikidata item to reach through one; Wikidata's own inventory of the series holds items for 53 of the 62 episodes, nine of the last ten having none at all; and of those items, three carry a duration — 23, 23 and 22 minutes. The series infobox does say "22 minutes", but that is one nominal figure for a 62-episode run and the three real durations are not all the same, so spreading it across every row would be a guess wearing a measurement's clothes. It is all rows or none, and a row with no weight on a weighted list silently counts as a full hour, so it is none.

Titles, numbering and airdates machine-read from Wikipedia's "List of Samurai Jack episodes" and "Samurai Jack season 5", with counts, dates, the numeral scheme and the fifth season's standing cross-checked against "Samurai Jack" and against Wikidata before this builds.

sections.intro: Thirteen years later and on a different network: ten episodes on Adult Swim's Toonami block, 11 March 2017 to 20 May 2017. The source files them as the fifth season of the same series, and their credited numerals jump to XCII to match the gap.
